o1.biggest_strength: It reads the data correctly: leads with dark spots and niacinamide, gives sunscreen its own objection-handling email, and builds slow-start guidance into the flow.
o1.biggest_mistake: It may be a little long and the Day 6 routine could push three products harder than a true beginner needs, though it does include a sensible slow-start plan.

o2.biggest_mistake: It invents a 14-day code expiry and builds fake urgency around it, and it uses off-brand/risky language such as “brightening” and stronger claims around salicylic acid.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Remove the unapproved expiry, clean up off-brand and medical-adjacent wording, and make the routine safer and slower for beginners.

reason: Output 1 is much closer to launch-ready for this brand: calmer, more compliant, and better aligned to the tracking gap and beginner fear. Output 2 has useful structure, but the invented deadline and off-brand wording would make me stop before sending it.
